deities: Maa Sheetla Devi (aradhya kuldevi of Rajnandgaon)
Kali, Bholenath (Shiva), Hanuman and Sai Baba within the same complex

history.dynasty: Bairagi Vaishnav rulers (per local press — period undocumented)
history.summary: Per local press (parwaztimes, March 2025), Rajnandgaon city has an ancient Sheetla Mata temple situated between the city's two major ponds, Rani Sagar and Budha Sagar, established in the time of kings and worshipped by the Bairagi Vaishnav rulers. Maa Sheetla is the aradhya kuldevi of Rajnandgaon — the first invitation to weddings, mundan and other auspicious occasions is offered to her — and the complex also houses Kali, Bholenath (Shiva), Hanuman and Sai Baba; devotees visit from far and wide, with special worship and nine days of bhajan-kirtan at Navaratri (Jyoti Kalash) and special puja on Diwali. AMBIGUITY: Justdial separately lists a 'Mata Sheetala Devi Shakti Peetha' at Basantpur, Rajnandgaon (daily 6 AM-1 PM), but its address line references the Badi/Chhotti Bambleshwari temples, which are at Dongargarh ~35 km away — this may be a different small shrine or a sloppy listing, and the two have not been reconciled. Documented here is the better-attested ancient city temple. Coordinates are a Rajnandgaon city approximation (no POI-level geocode match). Opening hours are not published — verify locally.

name: Maa Sheetla Devi Temple
town_description: Rajnandgaon, headquarters of its district on the Mumbai-Howrah rail route, is a commercial and cultural centre of western Chhattisgarh. Its old quarters cluster around historic ponds such as Rani Sagar and Budha Sagar, and it lies about 70 km from Raipur.

travel.railway: Rajnandgaon Junction, on the Mumbai-Howrah main line.
travel.road: In Rajnandgaon city on NH-53, near the Rani Sagar and Budha Sagar ponds.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; both Navaratris are the most festive times.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Hours are not published for the city temple — verify locally before travel.
